title: Not blaming conditioned capitalists: Goodman and Miles Davis
summary: Gil hesitates to blame people raised as capitalists, such as Goodman or Miles, since their music is beautiful.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Well this is I think what the values of this kind of, I don't think you can call it an interview because I'm having a marvellous time just sitting here talking to you. (LAUGHTER). But we need the insights that other people have.

I hesitate to really categorically nail people to the wall so the speak, because it's actually not their fault because they've been misrepresented since childhood anyway and they are raised as capitalists, right?

They are raised with that word of course, which is always touchy. Everybody gets nervous because they think if you say capitalists you are trying to promote communism which is just as bad, they go through that same routine. There are just different variations of different things, but it's basically no better.

And I mean, somebody like Benny Goodman or well anybody, Miles Davis, anybody, they are raised and conditioned to take, to play the game the way it's played. That's all. So you can't really nail anybody down for that and pick them out as, and blame them because their music is beautiful.

And blame them for not being avant garde in the economic world. You know, whatever other situation you may have, you know, if you like. To Blame them for not being hip on that, It's a waste of time because it's the way they are conditioned. It's done, right? It's been done already. It's done, the tape is formed the musculature is already formed the whole thing has been done.
